vocabulary.meaning_en: a word (because, unless, although, so that, before...) that starts a clause giving extra information
a sentence with a main idea plus a clause that gives more information
vocabulary.example: "I stayed home because I was sick" is a complex sentence.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a clause that can stand alone as a sentence
vocabulary.example: In "I like tea because it's hot", "I like tea" is the independent clause.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a clause that cannot stand alone; it adds information
vocabulary.example: "Because it's hot" is a dependent clause.
The concept is easy to understand.
The cause of the delay was the snow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that must happen so that something else can happen
vocabulary.example: You can go on one condition: be home by nine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a difference; something happens even though you expect it not to
looking at what is the same or different between things
the reason you do something; your aim
vocabulary.example: The purpose of the meeting is to plan the trip.
You can't have dessert unless you eat your vegetables.
Although it was raining, we played football.
She saved money so that she could buy a bike.
Call me as soon as you arrive.

fine_lines.title: because vs so that
fine_lines.explanation_ar: because يبيّن السبب (لماذا حدث الشيء). so that يبيّن الغرض (ما الذي تريد الوصول إليه).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Because gives the cause (why it happened). So that gives the purpose (what you want to get).

examples.sentence: Bitsy got dessert because she ate her carrots.
Bitsy ate her carrots so that she could have dessert.

fine_lines.title: if vs unless
fine_lines.explanation_ar: unless = if ... not (إلا إذا). You can't have dessert unless you eat = لا يمكنك إلا إذا أكلت.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Unless = if ... not. "You can't have dessert unless you eat your carrots" = if you don't eat them, no dessert.

examples.sentence: You can have dessert if you eat your carrots.
You can't have dessert unless you eat your carrots.

expressions.meaning_en: Starting a sentence with the reason (use a comma).
expressions.example: Because it was late, we took a taxi.
Although it was raining, we played outside.
Please reply as soon as possible.

expressions.meaning_en: What he says is partly true.
expressions.example: He said the test was too long. He has a point.

grammar.title: Simple vs complex sentences
grammar.explanation_ar: الجملة البسيطة: فاعل + فعل + مفعول (I like ice cream). الجملة المركّبة: جملة مستقلة + جملة تابعة تبدأ بأداة ربط تبعية لتضيف معلومات (I like ice cream because it tastes good).
grammar.explanation_en: Simple sentence: subject + verb + object (I like ice cream). Complex sentence: independent clause + dependent clause that starts with a subordinating conjunction and adds information (I like ice cream because it tastes good).
examples: When I get home, I'll have some ice cream. (complex)

grammar.title: C4 + P + T: what the conjunctions show
grammar.explanation_ar: Cause (السبب): because, since. Condition (الشرط): if, unless. Contrast (التباين): although, even though, while. Comparison (المقارنة): than, as...as. Purpose (الغرض): so that. Time (الزمن): after, before, when, while, since, until, as soon as, as long as.
grammar.explanation_en: Cause: because, since. Condition: if, unless. Contrast: although, even though, while. Comparison: than, as...as. Purpose: so that. Time: after, before, when, while, since, until, as soon as, as long as.
examples: Because Bitsy ate her carrots, she got dessert. (cause)
She can't have dessert unless she eats her carrots. (condition)
Although she was full, she ate dessert. (contrast)
Bitsy ate more dessert than anyone else. (comparison)
She ate her carrots so that she could have dessert. (purpose)
She had to eat her carrots before she could have dessert. (time)

grammar.title: Comma rule
grammar.explanation_ar: إذا بدأت الجملة بأداة الربط التبعية، نضع فاصلة بعد الجملة التابعة. الفاصلة تقول: هذه معلومة إضافية، والمعلومة المهمة بعدها. إذا جاءت أداة الربط في الوسط فلا نحتاج فاصلة عادة.
grammar.explanation_en: If the sentence starts with the subordinating conjunction, put a comma after the dependent clause. The comma says: this is extra information; the important part comes next. If the conjunction is in the middle, usually no comma.
examples: Although it was raining, we played soccer.
We played soccer although it was raining.

grammar.title: Time conjunctions must match the order
grammar.explanation_ar: لا تصلح كل أدوات الزمن في كل مكان؛ اختر الأداة التي تناسب ترتيب الأحداث: before للحدث الأول ثم الثاني.
grammar.explanation_en: Not every time word fits every sentence; choose the one that matches the order of events: before means this first, then that.
examples: She ate her carrots before she had dessert. ✔
She ate her carrots after she had dessert. (different meaning)

questions.question: You can't go out ___ you finish your homework.
___ it was raining, we played football.
She studied hard ___ she could pass the exam.
Where does the comma go?
choices: Because I was tired, I went to bed.
Because, I was tired I went to bed.
Because I was, tired I went to bed.
Because I was tired I, went to bed.
questions.explanation_en: The comma goes after the dependent clause.

questions.question: In "I stayed home because I was sick", which is the dependent clause?
questions.explanation_en: The dependent clause starts with the conjunction.

questions.question: Call me ___ you arrive at the airport.
questions.explanation_ar: زمن: as soon as = بمجرد أن.
questions.explanation_en: Time: as soon as = immediately when.

questions.question: What is a "concept"?
questions.explanation_en: A concept is a general idea.
